correctness.rationale: Condition on the first eligible deposited bond to establish the exact path recurrence and cycle decomposition; the Riccati equation and 0F1 quotient follow coefficient by coefficient. A strictly positive series for the denominator establishes a unique isolated minimal simple zero; its exact residue -1/alpha yields all-size exponential coefficient asymptotics. A quantitative convolution comparison proves strict root monotonicity, and analytic perturbation plus a sign bound establishes the 1/n hyperbolic-cosine crossover. Verified 35 independent exact finite-cycle Markov absorbing probabilities, 21 generating coefficients, two large-order pole estimates, and the root derivative numerically. Finite tests serve only as cross-checks.

originality.rationale: The claim is a full-coverage probability for unequal alternating edge clocks on a finite even cycle together with the hypergeometric pole law and finite-size symmetry crossover. The primary sources examined concern homogeneous vacancy laws, occupation marginals, sublattice mean coverages, and jamming-coverage scaling. None of the material actually inspected implies the inhomogeneous full-cover law or its 1/n symmetry crossover. Targeted published-finding corpus searches yielded only non-covering graph matching, unrelated pressure, and parity results. Inaccessible full texts retain genuine residual risk and are not asserted not to cover the claim.
residual_risks: Full text of Page (1959) was unavailable: homogeneous subcase may already be derivable from its complete vacancy distribution and is excluded from novelty.
Full text of Pippenger (1989) was unavailable; original abstract includes generic edge adsorption, so a hidden formula for a broader weighted process cannot be ruled out.
Full text of de Oliveira and Tome (1994) was unavailable; the paper studies inhomogeneity, though its abstract reports sublattice means rather than zero-vacancy probabilities.
Specialized non-indexed rare-event random greedy matching literature may contain equivalent alternating-weight formulas; the reported searches cannot logically prove absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: The statistic is the physically meaningful rare terminal event of full adsorption coverage, distinct from expected jamming density. Alternating bond adsorption rates model a patterned substrate and make two inequivalent perfect tilings compete dynamically; the theorem resolves their exact rare-event weights for every system size. The scale 1/n emerges from the competing exponential singularities and provides a nontrivial finite-size symmetry-crossover law. The new value is not a restatement of the known homogeneous Page vacancy recursion; it depends on the asymmetric rate-sensitive construction.
